slides.title: Things your doctor wishes you'd just ask

slides.q: Why do I feel dizzy after giving blood?
slides.a: Giving blood lowers your blood volume for a bit, and some people also have a reflex that drops their heart rate and blood pressure, which can make you lightheaded. That's why they have you rest, drink fluids and eat a snack after. Sitting or lying down usually fixes it fast. Tell the staff right away if you feel faint.

slides.q: Why do the glands in my neck swell when I'm sick?
slides.a: Those are lymph nodes, and they're part of your immune system. When you have a cold or sore throat, they fill up with immune cells fighting the infection, so they get bigger and tender. They usually shrink back within a few weeks. Worth seeing a doctor if one stays swollen, keeps growing, or feels hard and doesn't move.

slides.q: Why did I get a huge bump after hitting my shin?
slides.a: That's called a goose egg, and it's blood and fluid pooling under the skin after a hit. Your shin has very little padding, so swelling sticks out more there. Ice wrapped in a cloth helps it go down, and it may bruise as it heals. Worth seeing a doctor if you can't walk on it or the pain gets worse.

slides.q: Why do I see zigzag lights before a headache?
slides.a: That's often a migraine aura. Some people see flashing or zigzag lines, blind spots or shimmering for a few minutes, then a headache follows, though not always. It's worth getting checked so a doctor can confirm it and help you spot triggers. Get emergency help if it comes with weakness, numbness, confusion or trouble speaking.

slides.q: Why is the skin between my toes peeling?
slides.a: Peeling, itchy skin between the toes is very often athlete's foot, a fungal infection that loves warm, damp places like sweaty socks and gym showers. Drying well between your toes and changing socks daily helps a lot, and it's very treatable. Worth seeing a doctor if it cracks, spreads or hurts, or if you have diabetes.
